title: Highlighting the limited efficacy of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculectomy in Fuchs uveitis syndrome: a case series

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>); non-commercial and no-derivatives, therefore private

indication: uveitic (Fuchs uveitis syndrome related) open-angle glaucoma uncontrolled on multiple medications, adults under 50 years, unilateral disease; three of four eyes pseudophakic and vitrectomized after earlier phaco-PPV, one phakic; 360-degree gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT) as first glaucoma surgery; retrospective case series

groups.description: Four eyes of four patients with Fuchs uveitis syndrome glaucoma after 360-degree GATT; per-case values in Table 2 (columns Case 1 to Case 4)

series.notes: cells are 'IOP/number of medications'; the leading number is the IOP; rows 'Preop', '1 week', '2nd week', '1 month', '2 month', '3 month'; anterior chamber washout for hyphema within the first postoperative week, before the 1-week measurement (Case 1 text); second intervention (MMC trabeculectomy) at 8 months (Table 1 row R6)
cells are 'IOP/number of medications'; phakic eye; second intervention (MMC trabeculectomy) at 6 months (Table 1 row R6)

cells are 'IOP/number of medications'; poor medication adherence before surgery (text); steroids stopped in week 4; diode laser cyclophotocoagulation at the 3rd postoperative month (text; Table 1 row R6). The 3-month entry still lists glaucoma medications, whereas the text states the patient was off medication after cyclophotocoagulation, so the entry is read as preceding the second intervention; the article does not state this explicitly
cells are 'IOP/number of medications'; second intervention (MMC trabeculectomy) in the 4th month after GATT (text; Table 1 row R6)

exclusions.what: Number of medications (second number of each Table 2 cell) and Table 1 row R7
exclusions.reason: medication counts are mentioned in notes only (no medication series in schema 1.0.0)

exclusions.what: Table 1 (Tab1) other demographic and clinical rows
IOP values and IOP ranges given only in the case narratives (first postoperative day, ranges over weeks, values before the presenting visit and after the second interventions)
exclusions.reason: not table cells; ranges are not admissible; values after MMC trabeculectomy or cyclophotocoagulation belong to a different procedure

notes: Tonometer: not stated in the article ('At each visit, IOP was carefully measured').

Reference: preoperative IOP on glaucoma medication (Table 2 row 2 lists the medication count with the IOP; case narratives describe treatment under 3 to 4 molecules), recorded as preoperative_medicated.
Per-eye values exist, so individual series are extracted instead of a mean; each case is one eye.
Times: 1 week = 7/30.4375 months and 2nd week = 14/30.4375 months, rounded to 4 decimals.
Glaucoma medications were added sequentially after surgery when IOP exceeded the threshold stated in the Methods, so postoperative values are under varying medication.
